item.name: Twitching
item.warningSigns: Arms, head, or neck jerk while the patient is standing still. The back often hunches, and the neck can stretch longer than normal. Some variants only twitch on CCTV, so wait a few seconds before you decide.
item.bestAction: Close the shutters.
item.ifAdmitted: Often becomes a Shapeshifter during recovery, or can lead into a death ritual when paired with hollow eyes.
item.cardSummary: A patient that looks almost normal until the body starts twitching. Watch for a few seconds at the window before you stamp them in.

item.name: Three Eyes
item.warningSigns: Three slightly mismatched glowing red eyes sit where two normal eyes should be. The real eyes can still show underneath.
item.bestAction: Close the shutters.
item.ifAdmitted: Can trigger death rituals, monster events, or later transform into a Shapeshifter.
item.cardSummary: One of the easiest window checks. Extra glowing eyes mean this is not a real patient.

item.name: Hollow Face
item.warningSigns: Dark hollow eye sockets, often with a hunched posture and twitching. Looks drained and empty rather than injured.
item.bestAction: Close the shutters.
item.ifAdmitted: Strongly linked to death rituals during recovery. Not every hollow-eyed visitor is instantly hostile, but treating them as safe is a bad bet.
item.cardSummary: Empty sockets are the main tell. Do not confuse a normal sad face with fully hollowed eyes.

item.name: Realistic Face
item.warningSigns: Large eyes with black pupils, heavy under-eye bags, and a big drawn-on smile. The voice is often low and distorted.
item.bestAction: Close the shutters.
item.ifAdmitted: Can lead to death rituals, monster events, or a Shapeshifter transformation after check-in.
item.cardSummary: A fake face that looks hand-drawn or too human for a regular animal patient. The smile is usually the first thing that feels wrong.

item.name: Crooked Face
item.warningSigns: A crooked, distorted smile with sharp teeth and large mismatched eyes set high on the face. Eyes can look popped out.
item.bestAction: Close the shutters.
item.ifAdmitted: Can lead to death rituals, monster events, or a Shapeshifter transformation after check-in.
item.cardSummary: Uneven eyes and a sharp, crooked grin make this one stand out once you know what a normal patient face looks like.

item.name: X-rayed Face
item.warningSigns: Small but wide circular eyes with black pupils, paired with realistic human-looking teeth.
item.bestAction: Close the shutters.
item.ifAdmitted: Can lead to death rituals, monster events, or a Shapeshifter transformation after check-in.
item.cardSummary: The human teeth are the giveaway. A regular animal patient should not flash a full human smile at the desk.

item.name: Staring
item.warningSigns: The patient tracks your movement with their head, or locks onto a camera. The head can turn more than a normal patient should.
item.bestAction: Close the shutters.
item.ifAdmitted: Often turns into a Shapeshifter during recovery, so do not treat the intense eye contact as harmless.
item.cardSummary: If a patient keeps staring you down while you move around the desk, treat that as a hard reject.

item.name: Incorrect Photo
item.warningSigns: The finished polaroid does not match the patient at the window. The photo can swap features, markings, or show a face that is clearly not the same animal standing there.
item.bestAction: Wait for the photo to finish, compare it to the patient, then close the shutters if anything is wrong.
item.ifAdmitted: Admitting a photo mismatch can start a death ritual or later hostile transformation.
item.cardSummary: General photo mismatch. If the printed picture and the patient are not the same look, reject before you dig into which detail is wrong.

item.name: Different Eyes
item.warningSigns: The eyes in the photograph do not match the eyes on the living patient. Pupils, lids, shape, or eye style can all be wrong while the rest of the face looks close.
item.bestAction: Compare the photo to the patient before opening the shutters, then reject on any mismatch.
item.ifAdmitted: Same risk as other photo anomalies: ritual events or hostile forms later in the shift.
item.cardSummary: A common photo trap focused on the eyes. Side-by-side the window patient and the polaroid, and check the eyes first.

item.name: Different Ears
item.warningSigns: Ear shape, size, or animal type changes between the patient and the photo, such as bear ears on a rabbit patient.
item.bestAction: Check ear shape on both the patient and the finished photo before you admit them.
item.ifAdmitted: Same risk as other photo anomalies: ritual events or hostile forms later in the shift.
item.cardSummary: One of the sneakiest photo checks. Always look at the ears, not only the face.

item.name: Static Photo
item.warningSigns: The photograph has a grainy static overlay. It can appear alone or with other cursed photo details.
item.bestAction: Close the shutters when static covers the photo. Do not rely on tasing alone, especially on later shifts.
item.ifAdmitted: A static-only photo can still lead into a death ritual during recovery, even when it does not always become a Shapeshifter.
item.cardSummary: If the polaroid looks like a broken TV channel, do not stamp them in just because the window face looks normal.

item.name: Cursed Photo
item.warningSigns: The polaroid shows a heavily distorted or horrific face, such as a melted grin, wrong eyes, or other cursed face variants. Picking the photo up too early can also drain sanity.
item.bestAction: Let the photo fully develop, inspect it without rushing, then close the shutters.
item.ifAdmitted: A clear cursed face means a bad patient. Letting them through risks rituals and hostile forms.
item.cardSummary: These are the nasty polaroids. Wait for the print, check it on the desk, and shut the window if the face looks cursed.

item.name: Black Eyes
item.warningSigns: On the security camera, a black bar covers the face and realistic eyes stare back at you. The patient looks normal at the window and in the photo.
item.bestAction: Check CCTV before admission, then close the shutters.
item.ifAdmitted: Camera-only anomalies still count as real threats once they get past the desk.
item.cardSummary: A face that only looks wrong on the security feed. Window and photo can both be clean, so skip cameras at your own risk.

item.name: Unnatural Body
item.warningSigns: On CCTV the body looks stretched, warped, or detached, sometimes nicknamed boneless. Reopening the feed can change the shape again.
item.bestAction: Use lobby and check-in cameras, then close the shutters on any stretched body.
item.ifAdmitted: Camera-only body distortion is still an anomaly and can lead to later hostile outcomes.
item.cardSummary: If the limbs look longer than the hallway allows, reject them. Normal patients do not stretch like melted plastic.

item.name: Staring at Cameras
item.warningSigns: The patient keeps looking straight into the CCTV lens while walking or waiting, even when a normal patient would face the desk.
item.bestAction: Sweep the security cameras before admission and reject constant camera contact.
item.ifAdmitted: Camera-stare patients are still anomalies and can escalate after check-in.
item.cardSummary: Normal patients face the counter. Anomalies that live on camera feed keep staring into the lens instead.

item.name: Void Body
item.warningSigns: On the security camera the patient is a fully black silhouette with no normal color or detail.
item.bestAction: Close the shutters as soon as the feed shows a black void body.
item.ifAdmitted: A void silhouette is a clear anomaly and should never be treated as a normal patient.
item.cardSummary: If the camera turns the patient into a pure black figure, that is enough. No extra face check needed.

item.name: Camera Twitching
item.warningSigns: The patient only twitches on the security feed. At the window they may look completely still and normal.
item.bestAction: Leave the CCTV feed open for a few seconds before deciding the patient is safe.
item.ifAdmitted: Like other camera-only tells, this can still become a Shapeshifter or ritual problem after recovery.
item.cardSummary: Twitching that only shows on CCTV is easy to miss if you flick through cameras too fast.

item.name: Disguised Shapeshifter
item.warningSigns: Looks normal at the window, but security cameras show the true Shapeshifter form after the patient reaches the check-in spot. Lobby camera side views help. Twitching can appear only in that form.
item.bestAction: Check both lobby and check-in cameras once the patient reaches the window, then close the shutters.
item.ifAdmitted: You are letting a Shapeshifter into the hospital in disguise. It can attack patients and players after it drops the act.
item.cardSummary: The hard mode check-in. In person it looks fine. On camera it is already a monster waiting for a stamp.

item.name: Mismatching Ears
item.warningSigns: Ears or horns on the security camera do not match the ears you see at the window.
item.bestAction: Compare window ears to CCTV ears before admission, then reject any mismatch.
item.ifAdmitted: Subtle camera mismatches still count as anomalies and can escalate later.
item.cardSummary: A small ear change on CCTV is still a reject. This is one of the easiest tells to overlook when you rush.

item.name: Mismatching Eyes
item.warningSigns: Eye shape or style differs between the patient at the window and the same patient on CCTV.
item.bestAction: Zoom the lobby or check-in camera onto the face and reject any eye mismatch.
item.ifAdmitted: Subtle camera mismatches still count as anomalies and can escalate later.
item.cardSummary: Window eyes and camera eyes should match. If they do not, the patient is not real.

item.name: Head Banger
item.warningSigns: A hollow-eyed visitor smashes their head against the check-in glass and can block the shutters. This is not a normal queue patient.
item.bestAction: Offer coffee so they drink and leave. Avoid tasing, shooting, or forcing them out the hard way, which costs a large sanity hit.
item.ifAdmitted: Not a normal admit target. Handled at the window with coffee, not by treating them like a medical patient.
item.cardSummary: The window pest that wants coffee, not treatment. Feed it a cup and it calms down instead of wrecking your sanity.

item.name: Shapeshifter
item.warningSigns: A patient that has already dropped the disguise. Expect a huge mouth, sharp teeth, and an attack on nearby patients or players. Heavy breathing and copycat patients are early clues.
item.bestAction: Tase it, shoot it, or hold the interaction to pull it off a victim. If it grabs you, spam the struggle input.
item.ifAdmitted: This is the hostile form after a bad admit or transformation. It is already inside and needs a weapon response.
item.cardSummary: The end stage of a missed anomaly. Once the disguise drops, stop diagnosis mode and fight it before it eats a patient.
